claims.text: The catalyst is a PGM-based nanoscale catalyst with a defined surface structure and composition.
The initial catalyst is optimized for ethanol oxidation.
The electronic structure of surface atoms governs catalytic activity in ethanol oxidation.
The electronic structure of surface atoms governs product selectivity in ethanol oxidation.
Surface electronic structure modulates the adsorption strength of ethanol and its intermediates.
Changes in adsorption strength influence the ethanol-oxidation reaction pathway and product distribution.
Introducing a secondary metal such as gold or palladium can form a bimetallic alloy with the PGM catalyst.
Alloying with the secondary metal changes the electronic structure at the catalyst surface.
The dopant alters the d-band center of the PGM surface atoms.
A dopant-induced shift of the d-band center changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
Changes in adsorption energies alter the activation barriers of key ethanol-oxidation steps.
Changes in the activation barriers modify catalytic activity and selectivity.
Adding the dopant will measurably change the product distribution, potentially increasing selectivity toward acetic acid or acetaldehyde.
Adding the dopant will change the overall ethanol-oxidation rate.
The direction and magnitude of the rate and selectivity changes depend on the identity and concentration of the dopant.
The hypothesis should apply under mild to moderate temperatures and pressures where surface-mediated catalytic processes dominate.
The hypothesis may fail under extreme conditions where bulk diffusion or other non-surface effects become significant.
The undoped PGM nanoscale catalyst tested under the same reaction conditions is the experimental baseline.
